# TRACE-0001: security traceability

<!-- Written by the security-requirements-auditor. Do not edit by hand. -->

Requirements: appsec-baseline `requirements/security-requirements.md` (working tree; commit SHA not available to the auditor; SR-031 assessed with the amended text in SPEC-0001 §9)
Artifacts reviewed: SPEC-0001.md (stage: spec) with INT-0001.md and reviews/INT-0001-status.md as context (working tree; commit SHA not available to the auditor)

## Triggers
| Trigger | True? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| INPUT | true | The CI verifier, `classify.py`, `hash.py` and the gate parse review reports, file names and PR content that come from the PR (SPEC §2.2, §2.5); SPEC §9 itself treats reports as untrusted input. |
| ENDPOINT | false | No HTTP endpoint or served page is added or changed; no change to the dogs-app API or UI (INT-0001 Visual: none). |
| WRITE | false | No caller creates, changes or deletes application data. |
| FILE | false | No file upload, storage or serving in the app; review reports are small git-tracked JSON files (SPEC §2.2), not user file handling. |
| AUTHN | false | No change to how callers or operators are identified; the session keeps the owner's existing GitHub login (SPEC §4, owner decision 2026-10-28). |
| AUTHZ | true | SPEC §5 defines an authorisation matrix of actions by owner, main session, subagents and CI, enforced by hooks and GitHub. |
| CRYPTO | true | SHA-256 over file contents binds reports to files (SPEC §2.2, §9 SR-021). |
| DATA | true | Artifacts, reports, exceptions and logs are stored and transmitted; SPEC §6 inventories them (no personal data claimed). |
| LOG | true | SPEC §7 adds session summary lines and CI job logs and summaries. |
| SECRET | true | CI uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`; federation rules, service accounts and variables are removed (SPEC §4, §8). |
| DEP | true | New scripts and a reusable workflow; pinned tools and appsec-baseline lock (SPEC §2.1, §2.5, §2.6). |
| IAC | true | lab-admin `github.tf` changes (required checks, variables, labels, allowlist; SPEC §8). No AWS or IAM change. |
| CI | true | New `verify.yml`, `security.yml` changes, `deploy.yml` job removed (SPEC §2.5–2.7, §8). |
| AI | true | The whole change adds the local agent loop, agent tools, models and gate (SPEC §1, §2.3). |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| SR-001 | MUST | missing | SPEC §2.2, §9 | Schema has `additionalProperties: false`, a 256 KiB size limit, enums and `round` 1–3, but no max length or pattern for `model`, `files` keys, `file`, `evidence` or `recommendation`; no limit on array items; no UTF-8 or control-character rule; no Inputs table. See AUD-001. |
| SR-002 | MUST | missing | SPEC §9, §2.5 | States file names are data and `env` only, but not that report `files` keys are repo-relative and symlink-free before being opened, that subprocess calls take argument lists, that YAML is loaded safely, and has no named test. See AUD-002. |
| SR-003 | MUST | missing | SPEC §1.7 | INPUT is true, so the requirement applies. The verifier and `security-review.yml` post PR comments containing one-line evidence quoted from PR files; no text says the quoted text is escaped or neutralised. SPEC §9 lists SR-003 as not applicable. See AUD-003. |

See AUD-004. |

| SR-031 | MUST | covered | SPEC §1.3, §2.3, §5, §7, §9 | Allow lists, read-only reviewers, full model IDs, maxTurns, untrusted-input rule in every prompt, schema validation and escalation of invalid output and injection; amended no-merge-into-main text in §9. Evidence for model and maxTurns enforcement is weak (AUD-012). |

## Summary
Covered: 4 · Missing: 9 · N/A: 18

findings.evidence: §2.2 lists `model` as 'full model ID (2.3)' and `files` as 'path → SHA-256 hex'; the only size control is 'File size ≤ 256 KiB'. No max length, pattern, UTF-8 or control-character rule for strings, and no limit on number of `files` entries or `findings`.
findings.recommendation: Add an Inputs table for the report: max length and pattern per string (model, file paths, id, evidence, recommendation), valid UTF-8 and no control characters, maxItems for files and findings, and a test_report_schema_* case per rejected class.

findings.evidence: §9 SR-002: 'Verifier and scripts handle file names only as data (no shell interpolation; `env` only)'. Report `files` keys come from the untrusted PR and are opened to compute hashes; no rule on absolute paths, `..`, or symlinks, no safe YAML loading, no named test.
findings.recommendation: State that `files` keys must be repo-relative, inside docs/specs or the listed code paths, without `..` and not symlinks; subprocess calls use argument lists of fixed executables; YAML uses safe_load; add a named test (e.g. test_hash_rejects_path_outside_repo).

findings.evidence: §1.7: the CI comment lists 'ID, SR, file:line, one-line evidence, decision needed'. Evidence is quoted from PR content, an untrusted source, and nothing says it is escaped; §9 treats SR-003 as not applicable although INPUT is true.
findings.recommendation: Specify that untrusted text in PR comments is rendered as inert text (code span with backticks neutralised, no @mentions, no links or images, truncated to a stated length) and add a named test with a malicious evidence string.

findings.evidence: §5 matrix has cells 'make apply, terraform apply ... no (deny)', 'Edit .github/ ... yes (code stage only)', 'Edit ... stages.yml, appsec-baseline.lock ... ask', but §10 only names hook tests for subagent writes, `.claude/` ask and merge ask. Default-deny is not stated.
findings.recommendation: State that the hook and settings default to deny for anything not allowed in the matrix, and add a named test for every remaining cell (make apply deny, .github/ outside code stage, stages.yml and lock ask, TRACE/THREAT main-session-only, reviewer writes denied).

findings.evidence: §9 SR-021: 'SHA-256 over file contents, computed by `hash.py`; never git SHA-1 object IDs'. No mention of recording this use in the crypto inventory (lab-admin BASELINE), which SR-021 requires for every use of cryptography.
findings.recommendation: Add the BASELINE crypto inventory entry (SHA-256 report-to-file binding) to §8 clean-up and to the lab-admin PR scope.

findings.evidence: §2.5 step 2 uses the 'GitHub compare API' and step 3 checks out appsec-baseline; no statement that all connections use TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation enabled.
findings.recommendation: Add one line: all new connections (GitHub API, git, gh) use HTTPS only with certificate validation on; no --insecure, verify=False or http:// URLs; cover with the Semgrep TLS rules already run on code PRs.

findings.evidence: §6 data inventory lists git and 'GitHub Actions' as storage but does not say they are encrypted at rest (GitHub-managed) nor that Terraform state is unchanged by the lab-admin edits.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence in §6 stating GitHub-managed encryption at rest and that no new data store or Terraform state change is introduced.

findings.evidence: §7: 'Session: per stage one summary line (stage, round, verdict, findings count, model)'; 'CI: every check prints what it checked and the result to the job log'. No JSON Lines, no mandatory fields, no event names for denied hook actions or escalations, no never-logged list; EXC-001 does not cover SR-024 for these logs.
findings.recommendation: Define the log format for hook, gate and verifier events (JSON Lines with the SR-024 fields or the applicable subset, events such as authz.denied and input.rejected), list never-logged items (tokens, Authorization headers, presigned URLs, file contents), or record a lab exception with expiry.

findings.evidence: §6: '`redact.py` runs on every reviewer output before it's written'. `redact.py` is absent from the §2.1 script table and from §10; no patterns and no named test.
findings.recommendation: Add `redact.py` to §2.1, state what it redacts, and add named tests (e.g. test_redact_removes_token_patterns, test_redaction_escalates).

findings.evidence: §2.5: 'called from dogs-app `security.yml` job `verify` as `uses: …/verify.yml@main`'; the existing scanners job checks out appsec-baseline with `ref: main`. No hashed pin for the scripts' Python dependencies (jsonschema, YAML) and no SHA pins stated for actions in `verify.yml`.
findings.recommendation: Pin the reusable workflow and the scanners checkout to the lock SHA or document a justified deviation; install script dependencies with --require-hashes; pin every action in verify.yml by commit SHA from the BL-01 allowlist.

findings.evidence: §2.7: 'security-gate (= verify + scanners)'. The new job has no stated timeout-minutes, permissions or rule that a skipped or cancelled needed job fails the gate.
findings.recommendation: State for security-gate: permissions {}, timeout-minutes (at most 30), runs with always() and fails unless every needed job result is success; add a named test or actionlint check.

findings.evidence: §10 names only `test_agents_have_no_shell_or_network_tools` (parses every agent's frontmatter). No test asserts full model IDs, maxTurns and exact tool lists match §2.3; 'The main session runs on `claude-opus-5-5`' has no enforcement; the carried AUD-002 asked for named tests.
findings.recommendation: Add test_agents_match_spec_table (model, maxTurns, tools equal to §2.3, model is a full ID) and set the main-session model in committed project settings, covered by the same test.
